newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar weakness seen capped in Q2 - UBS.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar weakness seen capped in Q2 - UBS.

text.p: The Singapore dollar, under pressure against the U.S. dollar this year, could fall briefly as low as 1.45 but should recover to a 1.420-1.435 range through the second quarter, UBS Securities (Singapore) said on Thursday.
UBS said in a research bulletin a mildly weaker currency or further lay-offs could help alleviate the strain on Singapore manufacturers from two straight quarters of rising unit labour costs.
"Manufacturers have already cut payrolls in Q4 '96, and the government appears now to be doing its part by restraining the Singapore dollar's appreciation against its trade-weighted basket," it said.

Singapore's Finance Minister Richard Hu has said repeatedly in recent weeks the government was not concerned about the domestic currency's recent weakness against the U.S. dollar as it had remained fairly stable against a trade-weighted basket.
UBS said recent statements by Singapore officials also appeared to reflect a perception that local interbank rates were falling too rapidly.
"Hence the need to talk the local currency down, thereby causing liquidity to shrink by inducing some short-term capital outflow," it said.

"We believe that a three-month interbank rate of 2.75 percent is a level with which the authorities are comfortable," UBS said, adding it expected banks to cut their prime lending rates by 25 basis points before mid-1997.
The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4291/301 to the U.S. dollar in late trade on Thursday.
